title: GBrain
by: Garry Tan (Y Combinator); MIT licensed. Read from its README, its frozen memory protocol (docs/protocol/MEMORY_VERBS_v1.md), the system-of-record contract, the memory-boundaries guide and the coding-agent tutorial, all at raw.githubusercontent.com. Then its README on master, the memory-boundaries guide and the retrieval architecture (docs/architecture/RETRIEVAL.md) for links and timelines. The code and its benchmark were not read.
summary: A memory for agents kept as Markdown files in a git repo and indexed in Postgres for search. Agents reach it through one frozen set of seven verbs over MCP and the CLI: recall, remember, entity, synthesize, forget, context_pack and delta. Every write must carry its provenance, a fact is never deleted (it is superseded or withdrawn with a trail), and a conformance test checks that any server keeps the contract.
ideas: A frozen verb interface: field names and meanings in protocol v1 never change; new optional fields and new verbs are added without a version bump, and clients ignore what they don't know.
remember refuses a write with no provenance (error provenance_required); provenance is stored verbatim with the fact.

remember answers with a status to branch on: inserted, duplicate or superseded; a caller can name the fact it replaces with replaces, and the old fact is then expired with superseded_by, never deleted.
forget withdraws a fact from active recall but keeps it with an audit trail; remembering the same text again is refused (fact_withdrawn), so a withdrawal cannot be undone by accident.
Facts carry valid_from (when it became true) apart from created_at (when it was written); recall returns only active facts unless include_expired is asked for.
delta returns what changed since a cursor, so an agent that wakes up reads only the changes; delivery is at-least-once and the cursor never moves past what was delivered.
Errors have a few fixed codes and always carry a suggestion with the fix; a conformance command checks shape, contract behaviour and a remember-then-recall round trip, not ranking quality.
The git Markdown files are the system of record for pages; deletes in git become soft deletes in the index.

Links are found by a program, not a model: auto-link reads page references such as [[people/alice]] and stores them as edges; typed edges (works_at, invested_in, mentions) come from a fixed convention or a rule, and add_link adds one by hand.
A timeline entry can be added but never updated or removed; a page edit must quote the revision it read (expected_revision) or it is refused.
Forget expires a fact but keeps it; only an owner-only purge removes it, and no agent connection can call purge.

took.idea: One small frozen set of verbs, versioned and additive only
No write without an author and a source: refuse it with a fixed error code and a fix
A write says whether it inserted, duplicated or superseded, and names what it replaced
Withdrawal is its own act, kept in history, and blocks the same claim from coming back
A 'what changed since' read with a cursor
A conformance test for the interface itself
Links typed by the field they sit in, found by a program; links and backlinks returned by one read
Lists that only grow, and edits that quote the version they read
